articles.title: Motion-Preserving Salvage for Failed Total Ankle Arthroplasty or Talar AVN: Outcomes of Combined Total Ankle Arthroplasty with Custom 3D-Printed Total Talus Replacement.
articles.authors: Saggar R, Smith RM, Heidinger E, Yaldo OM, Hasselman CT, Hogan MV, et al.
articles.population: Patients with talar component collapse after total ankle arthroplasty or talar avascular necrosis with ankle and subtalar arthritis
articles.sample_size: 18 patients (10 female, 8 male; mean age 57.8 years)
articles.outcomes: Complication rate 33.3%, reoperation rate 11.1%, functional recovery milestones (controlled ankle motion at 19.9 days, full weight-bearing at 46.9 days, regular footwear at 10.7 weeks), radiographic osseointegration achieved in all patients
articles.take_home: Combined total ankle replacement with custom 3D-printed talus replacement is a motion-preserving option for salvaging failed ankle replacement or severe talar damage, with acceptable complication rates and rapid functional recovery, though careful patient selection is important.

articles.title: Three-Dimensional Osseous Alignment and Morphology Patterns of Ankle and Hindfoot Osteoarthritis.
articles.authors: Lapins ER, Peterson AC, Mills MK, Saltzman CL, Lenz AL
articles.study_type: Retrospective cross-sectional study using 3D computed tomography imaging
articles.population: Patients with ankle and hindfoot osteoarthritis and non-osteoarthritic controls
articles.sample_size: 196 weightbearing CT scans (130 osteoarthritis patients, 66 controls)
articles.outcomes: 3D bone shape and alignment patterns; joint space narrowing; classification of osteoarthritis presentations (subtalar only, ankle only, combined) by foot alignment type
articles.take_home: Different types of ankle and hindfoot osteoarthritis show distinct 3D alignment patterns linked to foot shape, with ankle-only disease associated with high arches and combined disease showing the most variable presentations. This suggests the foot and ankle work as an interconnected system, and assessing both together may better understand how osteoarthritis develops and progresses.

articles.title: Which factors are associated with failure of conservative treatment in progressive collapsing foot deformity?
articles.authors: Micicoi L, Grun W, Luo E, Bryniarski A, Pozzessere E, Umrethiya V, et al.
articles.population: Adults with progressive collapsing foot deformity initially treated without surgery
articles.outcomes: Factors associated with needing surgery despite non-operative treatment: hindfoot malalignment, male sex, and higher BMI
articles.take_home: People with progressive collapsing foot deformity who have worse hindfoot alignment, are male, or have a higher BMI were more likely to need surgery despite starting with non-operative treatment. Pain levels at the start did not predict who would need surgery.

articles.title: The effect of tibial rotational deformity on ankle joint loadings: A finite element analysis.
articles.authors: Bolukbasi AET, Kocadal O, Aksu BC, Yuksel K, Yardimci K
articles.population: Simulated distal tibial shaft fractures treated with intramedullary nailing
articles.sample_size: 7 computer models (neutral alignment plus 6 malrotation scenarios)
articles.outcomes: Tibiotalar cartilage stress and implant stress under axial loading
articles.take_home: When the tibia heals in a rotated position after nail fixation, it puts extra stress on the ankle cartilage, with inward rotation causing more damage than outward rotation. This could increase the risk of ankle wear and tear over time.

articles.title: Multi-segment foot kinematics in talocalcaneal coalition: A radiologically matched case-control study.
articles.authors: Kim WS, Jeong D, Park MS, Sung KH
articles.population: People with talocalcaneal coalition compared to matched controls without coalition
articles.sample_size: 18 feet with coalition matched 1:1 to 18 control feet
articles.outcomes: Multi-segment foot kinematics during gait, including hindfoot, forefoot, hallux and arch length motion
articles.take_home: People with talocalcaneal coalition have reduced dynamic arch movement during walking compared to those without the condition, but other foot movements remain similar. The ankle joint appears to compensate for the restricted movement between the heel and other foot bones.

articles.title: Accuracy of implant positioning in total ankle arthroplasty using patient-specific instrumentation: A weightbearing CT analysis of landmark-based parameters.
articles.authors: Garibaldi R, Lama JE, Henry JK, Lan R, Demetracopoulos CA, Ellis SJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing total ankle arthroplasty with patient-specific instrumentation
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of implant positioning measured by distance from anatomical landmarks and angular alignment of talar component on weightbearing CT scans
articles.take_home: Patient-specific instrumentation for ankle replacement was accurate for most positioning measurements within 1 mm, though about one in five medial measurements and some talar angles varied more than planned. The system worked well overall but sagittal talar alignment was less reliable than distance-based positioning.

articles.title: Distribution and Treatment Patterns of Symptomatic Tarsal Coalition in Japan: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.authors: Matsui T, Sugimoto K, Miura K, Isomoto S, Samoto N, Kumai T, et al.
articles.population: Patients diagnosed with symptomatic tarsal coalition in Japan
articles.sample_size: 127 coalitions identified across 4 specialized foot and ankle centres
articles.outcomes: Types of tarsal coalition and their treatment patterns. Talocalcaneal coalitions were most common (56.7%), followed by naviculocuneiform (22.8%) and calcaneonavicular (16.5%). Conservative treatment succeeded in 33.1% of cases; surgical treatment was used in 66.9%, with coalition resection in 60.6% and arthrodesis in 6.3%.
articles.take_home: In Japanese patients with painful tarsal coalitions, talocalcaneal fusion was the most common type, differing from patterns traditionally seen in Western populations. Most patients required surgery, with removal of the coalition being more common than joint fusion.

articles.title: Perioperative Factors Associated With Postoperative Failure-Free Survival After Arthrodesis for Diabetic Charcot Neuroarthropathy of the Foot or Ankle.
articles.authors: Wang Q, Zhang Y, Shen S, Wang J, Wang JH, Zhao HM
articles.population: Patients with stage III diabetic Charcot neuroarthropathy of the foot or ankle treated with arthrodesis
articles.outcomes: Postoperative failure-free survival at 6 and 12 months following arthrodesis
articles.take_home: Just over half of patients (58%) remained stable at 12 months after foot or ankle fusion surgery for Charcot neuroarthropathy. Patients with longer diabetes duration and those who smoke had worse outcomes, whilst blood sugar control levels did not independently predict success.

articles.title: Unilateral CT systematically overestimates syndesmotic malreduction: Clinical implications of bilateral CT assessment after ankle fracture fixation.
articles.authors: Van Der Velden B, Campbell J, Jadav B, Doornberg J, Jaarsma R
articles.population: Patients who underwent ankle fracture fixation with syndesmotic stabilisation
articles.outcomes: Classification of syndesmotic reduction status using unilateral versus bilateral CT imaging; rate of disagreement between imaging methods
articles.take_home: Using only one-sided CT scans incorrectly suggested the ankle was not properly aligned in nearly 12% of cases, whereas looking at both sides gave a more accurate picture. Doctors should consider bilateral CT scans when deciding whether revision surgery is needed.

articles.title: Clinical determination of forefoot morphotypes in flexible Charcot-Marie-Tooth cavovarus feet - A novel system of clinical examination.
articles.authors: Malhotra K, Matheron G, Aggarwal A, Patel S, Cullen N, Welck M
articles.population: People with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease and cavovarus feet deformity
articles.sample_size: 60 feet (30 feet also had weightbearing CT imaging)
articles.outcomes: Agreement between clinical examination and CT-based software categorisation of forefoot morphotype; inter-rater reliability between two clinicians
articles.take_home: Doctors can reliably identify different types of cavovarus foot shape using clinical examination alone, which could help surgical planning for patients who cannot access CT scanning. The study found very high agreement between clinical assessment and imaging-based categorisation.

articles.title: The association between surgeon grade and clinical outcome in fourth-generation minimally invasive hallux valgus surgery.
articles.authors: Lau B, Newton A, Lewis TL, Vignaraja V, Franklin S, Trowbridge S, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing minimally invasive surgery for hallux valgus (bunions)
articles.outcomes: Radiographic measurements (hallux valgus angle, intermetatarsal angle, distal metatarsal articular angle), patient-reported outcome measures (MOXFQ and EQ-5D-5L), and complication rates
articles.take_home: Trainee surgeons performing minimally invasive bunion surgery under direct supervision achieved results comparable to experienced consultant surgeons, with similar improvements in X-ray measurements, patient satisfaction scores, and complication rates.
